subject: Request: Hosted API latency commitments & temporary p95 carveout during migration
messages:
From: Maya Patel <ops@brightline.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commitments — migration window needs

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're ramping an infra migration next month that will shift 30–40% of our traffic across regions for ~72 hours. Legal has asked us to confirm the p50/p95 commitments for the hosted API during that window and whether Redwood can offer a temporary carveout for p95 while traffic stabilizes.

Specifically:
- Current contract: p50 = 80ms, p95 = 350ms (measured 1h rolling window)
- Migration expectation: sustained 3x peak in a 6–12 hour burst, then tailing load for 48–72 hours

Can you:
1) Confirm how measurement windows and sampling would apply for that migration period?
2) Tell us if Redwood will grant a time-limited p95 relief (and how that would show up in SLA reporting)?
3) Share what evidence/audit artifacts you can provide post-migration (logs, percentile proofs, dashboards)?

We need this for our procurement & legal teams to sign off on the maintenance window. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Ops, Brightline Health
attachments: none

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <ops@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — migration window needs

Maya — thanks for the heads up and the clear breakdown. Short answers up front: we can provide a temporary, documented carveout for p95 tied to a defined migration window; measurement will be explicit and auditable; we can provide an evidence package afterward.

Notes / proposed approach:
- Measurement: shift from our default 1h rolling window to a 24h aggregated window for the affected days (this is to avoid penalizing short, high-amplitude bursts). We will still capture minute-level metrics for your audit.
- Carveout: propose a time-boxed exception (start/end timestamps you confirm) where p95 is exempt from SLA crediting for the duration plus a short recovery buffer (6 hours). We will record the carveout in the SLA addendum and in our incident ledger.
- Observability artifacts: minute-level latency CSV, per-region p50/p95 time series, request traces for sampled sessions, and our measurement script (so you can reproduce).

Action items I propose:
1) Brightline to confirm exact migration start/end windows (UTC).
2) Redwood to provide a signed SLO carveout addendum + evidence checklist (attaching a template).
3) Post-migration: Redwood will deliver the evidence package within 5 business days and offer a 1-hour review call.

Attaching: SLO_exception_template.pdf (template for carveout addendum).

If that sounds workable I'll loop in Legal/Contracts to formalize.

—Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
attachments: SLO_exception_template.pdf

From: Maya Patel <ops@brightline.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — migration window needs

Thanks Jonas — that high level is fine. A few clarifying questions from procurement & security:

- For the 24h aggregation idea, will you still count per-minute samples toward any monitoring alerts we have tied to our SLAs? We want to avoid missing a real regression while not triggering SLA credits for expected migration noise.
- Can you confirm the exact artifact list you will deliver (file names/formats)? Procurement wants to know if we can ingest the CSV into our analytics pipeline automatically.
- One more ask: can you include a signed statement that the carveout will not be used to mask sustained degradations beyond the migration window?

If you can answer these in the addendum and provide an example CSV header, procurement can sign off quickly. We have the migration tentatively scheduled for 2026-08-03 22:00 UTC to 2026-08-06 04:00 UTC.

Maya
Brightline Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <ops@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments — migration window needs

Maya — great, thanks for the dates. Quick replies inline then an attachment and links below.

- Monitoring vs SLA: we'll keep your monitoring/alerting intact — minute-level alerts continue to fire. The carveout only exempts SLA credit calculations for the p95 percentile for the stated window + 6h buffer. Any sustained degradation passing your alert thresholds is still actionable and will trigger our incident process. (We will add this explicitly to the addendum.)

- Artifacts: we will deliver the following, all machine-readable:
  • latency-evidence-sample.csv (CSV; header below)
  • per-region-p50p95.json (JSON time-series)
  • minute-sampled-traces.log (ndjson, sampled at 1/100 requests)
  • signed-carveout-addendum.pdf (PDF)

Example CSV header (first row):
"timestamp_utc,region,request_id,route,p50_ms,p95_ms,request_count,success_rate"
- Statement of non-abuse: yes — we will include an explicit clause: "Carveout applies strictly to the window recorded in the addendum. Any extended or repeated performance anomalies outside that window will be evaluated under the standard SLA and remediation process." We'll have Legal draft and sign.

Next steps:
1) I'll draft the signed addendum using the template and circulate it for countersignature by EOD tomorrow (2026-07-21).
2) After your migration completes, expect the evidence package within 5 business days and an optional review call; we'll upload artifacts to a shared Drive folder and add a HubSpot note (HS-987654).

If you want the addendum to call out the 24h measurement aggregation explicitly by UTC dates, reply-all with any edits; otherwise I'll push the first draft tomorrow.

—Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
attachments: latency-evidence-sample.csv
